messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: P1 - latency_p95_slo_violation for route /v1/generate in us-west-2. p95=720ms (>500ms). Paging @oncall-sre and @eng-runtime.

aj: oncall here, picking this up. Can someone drop the dashboards and recent deploys?

lina: dashboards - huge spikes from traffic shard A starting ~12:03 UTC. I'm seeing immediate reroutes to us-east-1 and then back to us-west-2 in ~90-150s intervals. Feels like a bounce loop.

devon: that matches what I see in routing traces: route decision flips based on p95 threshold, then backend warms up and p95 drops, triggers flip back.

sam: pulling routing-policy config now.

sam: ```yaml
policy: latency_based_fallback
threshold_ms: 500
cool_down: 0s
variant_selector: auto
region_fallback: [us-east-1, eu-west-1]
```

aj: cool_down=0s?? we intended a cooldown of 180s for that policy. Who rolled that?

lina: I just remembered: there was an experiment toggle "fast-failover" we flipped in the morning to reduce failover latency. It had a config override but we expected the feature flag to be scoped to staging.

devon: can someone run the routing debug for a sample request trace id 0x7f9a4? I want to see decision timeline.

aj: running `redwoodctl debug trace 0x7f9a4 --route /v1/generate` ->```
2026-03-15T12:05:22Z route_decision: us-west-2 (p95 720ms)
2026-03-15T12:05:23Z fallback_decision: us-east-1 (policy: latency_based_fallback)
2026-03-15T12:05:25Z return_to_primary: us-west-2 (p95 dropped to 380ms)
2026-03-15T12:07:40Z fallback_decision: us-east-1 (p95 spiked again)
```

aj: also seeing model variant flip on fallback: primary was `gptx-3-bf16`, fallback is `gptx-3-4bit-mut`. That variant is missing native function_call support.

anna: logs from gateway show a small but notable error class: `tool_call_not_supported` and some 502s for requests requiring function/tool calls. Correlates with the times of fallback.

sam: customer impact footprint: top 3 accounts by traffic saw increased latencies; 0.2% of overall requests returned 502 during the window. CS note: ACME, BeaconHealth, Eduify.

aj: immediate mitigation plan: 1) freeze routing policy (prevent further automatic fallbacks) 2) set cool_down to 300s 3) pin model_family for fallback to the compatible bf16 variant 4) rollback the "fast-failover" scope to staging.

devon: agreed. I'll own the routing freeze and variant pin. aj, can you patch the policy?

aj: doing the changes now. Running: `redwoodctl set routing-policy latency_based_fallback --cool_down 300s --variant_selector "family==gptx-3-bf16" --apply`

deploy-bot: ROUTING POLICY UPDATE: latency_based_fallback updated by aj at 2026-03-15T12:14:02Z.

sam: cancelling the experiment rollout: `featurectl rollback fast-failover --env prod` -> success.

aj: monitoring. p95 in us-west-2 trending down to ~420ms. reroutes reduced to 1 per 15m (previously every 90-150s).

lina: verifying model compatibility - fallback now pinned to `gptx-3-bf16` family; no more tool_call errors in the sample window.

devon: preliminary impact assessment: total requests affected ~0.2%, request latency increase for some customers peaked at +220ms p95. No data exfiltration, no SLA breach escalations yet.

product-ops: CS will draft a short note to ACME/BeaconHealth/Eduify outlining impact and mitigation. Postmortem owner?

devon: I'll own the postmortem. Actions: (A1) Add validation gate preventing cool_down=0 for latency policies (A2) Add model-variant compatibility check before routing (A3) Add tighter rollout gates for "fast-failover" experiment to prevent global staging leak.

aj: leaving oncall for 1hr for observation. Handing off to devon at :12:30 UTC.

lina: adding to incident runbook: ensure `cool_down >= 60s` and that variant_selector cannot be empty.

aj: thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated for now. Will update when we have the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
